subject: fpeaks for a 2D-spectrogram instead of a spec or meanspec?

messages.author: 48217e53baa77b47
messages.subject: fpeaks for a 2D-spectrogram instead of a spec or meanspec?
parts:
I'm trying to obtain the frequency/amp peaks over time in a wav file. If I use fpeaks() on a spec or meanspec, I get a histogram of frequency and amplitude. Instead what I want is a plot (and list) of the peak frequencies over time (ideally limited to some number/second but I can deal with whatever). So, time on the X, freq on the Y, and choose which ones to plot based on peak amplitude of the frequencies.

The spectro() function gives me a plot that is almost what I'm looking for. It plots freq over time and uses color intensity to represent amplitude values. I basically want a plot of that same information, but just a curve of the highest amplitude points.

Is this possible with seewave?

Best wishes,

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] fpeaks for a 2D-spectrogram instead of a spec or meanspec?
parts:
Hi,

I think this is possible with seewave. If i understand what you wanna do is:
-calculate fpeaks for all your successive recordings
-plot your results along a time scale (representing your recording times)

I would suggest a loop that first detect your frequential peaks using
fpeaks(), then you can consider the other frequency as zero (so put
zero for each of your frequency not detected by fpeak) and then,
create a matrix with your frequency in row and recording in column,
use the function rbind() to simply paste your frequency vectors in
each column of the matrix). You should now be able to plot this matrix
as a spectogram and be able to design this function as you like (look
into the code of spectro to reproduce the plot parameters that you like)

Hope this help!

Amandine
